details:
Not sure if I'm using the correct terminology, but a feature similar to Nvidia Shadowplay or the Switch's recording feature might be able to be implemented with minimal performance impact, 

This buffer would be continuously updated and rewritten in the background as you play and then through some button, perhaps in the camera menu or quick menu, would save a file to a folder (similar to how photos are handled) that stores the latest version of the buffer, 

The buffer could be locally handled on the system perhaps with different modes depending on hardware, with quest storing a lower frame rate and resolution perhaps with a shorter buffer too, of a minute/30 secs/etc. 

These recordings could also be used as an option when filling out reports as most behavioural related report options require additional proof that usually requires going on the website and other things that increase the friction and lower the chance of a report actually being completed, this could work by allowing the use of the buffer when in the report menu, 

The only time that buffer contents would impact VRC's server capacity would be when they are sent alongside reports, if VRChat holds proof used in reports usually, 

Any other use for buffers would be local to the user's device and VRChat would never lay their eyes on them unless shared in a report or elsewhere online, 

This leads into the second purpose of buffers, smoother social media output for viral content, etc. with a native and easy to use video recording format it could increase the amount of content surrounding the game online, bringing another wave of new players to the game and allowing further growth of the platform as a whole, 

Buffers as a whole could be moderated through different types of instances, perhaps being suspended in instance types considered private, though in public instances, I would make the case that anyone could be recording anyway and, as a native solution, it does not have to be mandatory and it could have a signifier to other users that it is active, similarly to how earmuff mode is shown on the nameplate of a player with it activated, 

Additionally, clips from buffers could perhaps be integrated into the inventory similar to how prints are handled now, with proper resolution caps and frame rate limits as this would take up VRC's server capacity, these could perhaps act as prints but have an animated, looping GIF created from a buffer, 

A small video cropping tool could be created for in-game use that would be used to create these clips, it could also be used within reports but the raw unedited buffer would be ideal to ensure the most context, 

I understand that this is wordy and long-winded, but I believe a feature like this would be a net good for the platform as a whole as long as it could be implemented in a way that doesn't negatively affect performance, especially on hardware like the Quest in standalone mode, it could also be entirely optional if one does not find it to be worth the trade-off
title: Rolling Buffer POV Integrated For Better Safety As Well As Outreach On Social Platforms
